title: Where did dharma go?
hookLine: the sages ask where dharma went when Krishna left, and the Bhagavata answers
carry: when krishna left, dharma sheltered in his word
tomorrow: Sam says 'so the Buddha was a Hindu god.' Dawa goes quiet. now what?

lines: WHERE HAS DHARMA GONE FOR SHELTER?
cards: Some people keep an old voicemail from someone they've lost, just to hear the voice again. The Bhagavata Purana opens near a question like that.

Sages have gathered in the Naimisha forest for a long ritual, and they ask the storyteller, Suta: Krishna, the protector of dharma, has gone back to his own home. So where has dharma gone for shelter now?

teach.b: Suta's answer takes the whole Purana, but he gives it in one picture near the start.

teach.h: THIS PURANA RISES LIKE THE SUN.
teach.b: Now that Krishna has gone home, this Purana has risen like the sun, for people in the Kali age who have lost their sight. Hear what that claims. When Krishna left, he didn't leave nothing behind.
His stories stayed. Many devotees honor the Bhagavata as Krishna himself, in words.

teach.h: HEARING IS A WAY OF MEETING.
teach.b: At a Bhagavata saptaha, a seven-day recitation, the book is often carried in procession and given a seat of honor, and people sit for hours to hear it, because in this tradition hearing about God is a way of meeting God.
Prahlada even names hearing first among the ways of devotion. So look back at what we heard this week. Rama's open door.
The baby carried through the rain. One line: the others are portions, but Krishna is the Lord himself, krishnas tu bhagavan svayam. Yuge yuge: he comes whenever dharma slips.
Don't be afraid: grace for the hunter.
And the Buddha, to whom the Bhagavata gives one short verse, born among the Kikatas at the start of the Kali age, a verse readers still argue over, while Jayadeva sang his compassionate heart.

teach.h: THE WEEK: MANY FACES, ONE LORD.
teach.b: Many faces, one Lord coming down, and the stories are how he stays close. Notice the sages' word, too: shelter. On the beach, Vibhishana came to Rama for shelter.
Here, dharma does, in the word. So when a grandmother plays a Bhagavata katha in the kitchen, in this reading she isn't only remembering Krishna. She's keeping him company.

how: At a Bhagavata saptaha, a seven-day recitation, the book is often carried in procession and given a seat of honor; many Hindus touch a holy book to the forehead before reading it.

o: a king of the Kikatas who fought the gods' enemies
named in one Bhagavata verse, born among the Kikatas
a sage who taught at the start of the Kali age

games.q: the week, person by person — tap the pairs.
p: came for refuge and was taken in
asked where dharma went for shelter
told: don't be afraid, get up
where the Bhagavata places the Buddha's birth

s: the Bhagavata tells the Buddha's whole life story
it gives him one verse: when, whose son, where, and why.
Hindu texts give the Buddha more than one face
the Bhagavata's verse and Jayadeva's compassionate heart are very different tellings.
the Bhagavata says nothing was left once Krishna went home
it says this Purana rose like the sun for people in the Kali age.

games.q: your little cousin asks: if Krishna left the world long ago, how can we still know him?
o: his stories stayed. in the Bhagavata, hearing them is a way of meeting him.
we can't. he's gone, so the stories are just history now.
only priests can reach him now; everyone else has to wait.
games.why: the sages asked where dharma went when Krishna left. Suta's answer is the Purana itself, risen like the sun for the Kali age.

practice: If there's a holy book in your home, the Gita, the Ramayana, any, hold it a moment and touch it to your forehead, the way many Hindus do. Then set it in front of you and breathe slowly.
If you don't keep one, hold any book that has mattered to you. Let the week's pictures pass once: a beach at night, a prison door, a conch, an arrow. Then rest in the quiet.

wordCard.voice: Buddha: in the Bhagavata, one verse, born among the Kikatas at the start of the Kali age; in Jayadeva, a compassionate heart.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: when Krishna left, dharma took shelter in his word. The stories are how he stays. A week ends here.
